description:
Reclassified from the fz-kdt.107 review addendum (2026-09-01): on
00277 under LIFO, Kernel.dbg/1[empty_list()] is minted and shipped
beside Kernel.dbg/1[list(int)] -- the first key's ENTIRE domain is
contained in the second's, same function, and nothing dedups keys.
This is NOT fz-kdt.106's class (its dominance is row-scoped within one
activation key by construction) and not dispatch-order (fz-kdt.107):
it is an unowned question about key-level subsumption at specialization
minting. It is also schedule-visible (the empty_list() key exists under
LIFO only on 00277 -- half of that fixture's 180-vs-181 residue).
Direction to weigh when picked up: dedup at mint (canonical_activation_
key answering the contained key with the container -- but beware
fz-kdt.80's lesson that key equality != emission idempotence, and
fz-y6w's that per-key precision is usually the point: a contained key
with NARROWER lanes may be the better executable; subsumption may be
the wrong direction entirely and the real cure demand-side). Measure
the population first: how many contained-key pairs exist corpus-wide.

comments.text: Data point from fz-kdt.132 (c31b309d0), which this ticket was named as a neighbour of. The take_drop 'cross-key subsumption smell' this ticket's neighbourhood was suspected of was NOT subsumption: the three same-function accumulator keys ({[], []}, {[], [int]}, {[], [int]} | {[int], []}) were a truncated ASCENT LADDER, not redundant siblings. Deduping them by containment would have been the wrong cure -- the right one minted the rung above them and the ladder collapsed to a single key on its own (three reducer specializations per captured lambda became one, 00420 215 -> 196 executables). Worth re-measuring 00277's Kernel.dbg/1[empty_list()] vs Kernel.dbg/1[list(int)] pair against HEAD before building: the population this ticket asks to count may have moved.

title: Cross-key specialization subsumption: an executable whose whole domain is contained in a same-function sibling is minted and kept
